page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 16 vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture. The system features a shared CPU allocation model running on a KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, containing 24 GB of VRAM. This server does not include local storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded gzip compression both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is strong, with stress-ng multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 25%. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth is also strong at 223.85 GB/sec. For machine learning workloads, the system achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 339.34 tokens per second on a small 135M parameter LLM, while prompt processing speeds fall in the average tier.

The server presents a qualitative balance between high-capacity memory and GPU acceleration, though the shared CPU allocation model represents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, isolated CPU performance. The lack of bundled local storage requires external storage attachments. This configuration is suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as small-scale LLM inference, data science tasks, and memory-intensive parallel processing applications that benefit from the 192 GB memory footprint and Ada Lovelace GPU architecture.
